column1: PCC-01
column3: the profile contract: admissibility, answerability, and the basis of a particular value
column5: profiles.yaml ranked SOURCES and said nothing about the BASIS of a value. A modern-critical figure reprinted in a Catholic reference work arrived as traditional chronology because of the shelf it stood on, and the rule that actually decided several withdrawals -- that section 4.3's reporting licence is granted to Ussher by name and to nothing else -- existed only as a silence the corpus cited as if it were text.
column6: profiles.yaml carries an `admissibility` block: fifteen named basis classes, seven admissible and eight not; the two-question rule (is the SOURCE admissible, then is the BASIS OF THIS VALUE admissible) asked in that order and BEFORE rank; an `own_voice` clause saying publication context is not a basis; a `preservation` clause saying refusing a basis is not an instruction to delete; and one narrow, named `reporting_exceptions` entry for Ussher whose narrowness is machine-enforced. Plus an `answerability` block making answerable-vs-preserved an axis orthogonal to disposition.

A reviewer reading the profile and a reviewer reading the rulings got two different policies, and the second was discoverable only by reading code and notes. column6: `rule` states the disclosure test in terms: the basis test asks WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS THE VALUE RESTS ON, and refuses a value the work carrying it PRESENTS as resting on an excluded method. column6: Both stand, and both now argue it in their own notes, under the profile's `corroboration_is_not_the_ground` clause, which requires a claim reading a named warrant as corroborative to SHOW the admissible ground it says is primary. Agrippa: Howlett's sentence puts Josephus first and the coinage after him under one hedge, and Prat's "St. Paul" reaches the same year 44 from Acts and Josephus alone, naming no coin -- "in the third year of his reign, which had begun in 41 (Josephus, 'Ant.', XIX, vii, 2)", "These combined facts bring us to the year 44" -- so the corpus would carry A.D. 44 on that sentence alone. WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE is stated in the same clause: a rejection made on a ground this profile ADMITS reaches the figure, and `rejected-by-source` is the class for it. At the Baptism the article's own sentence adopts Ramsay's reckoning of Tiberius's years and OBTAINS A.D. 27 from it, so the disclosed warrant of the value is the excluded reckoning. This solution is offered to obviate apparent discrepancies between Galatians 2 and Acts 15" -- maintained by a Catholic professor whose arguments the article summarises, asserted in antiquity by Marcion, and concurred in by Ramsay. He is named as one who holds the position, not as the warrant it rests on, and no lift is invoked. The basis now quotes the grounding sentences too.
